reading.title: Marine Ecosystem Resilience and Ocean Acidification
reading.passage:
Ocean acidification, caused primarily by increased atmospheric carbon dioxide absorption, represents one of the most significant threats to marine ecosystems worldwide. When CO₂ dissolves in seawater, it forms carbonic acid, which lowers the ocean's pH and reduces the availability of carbonate ions essential for shell-forming organisms. This process, occurring at an unprecedented rate of 0.1 pH units per decade, undermines the calcification processes in pteropods, corals, and mollusks, potentially destabilizing entire food webs.

Recent studies indicate that the physiological stress induced by acidification extends beyond calcification challenges. Many organisms exhibit impaired sensory capabilities and behavioral changes even at modest pH reductions, suggesting that neural systems are particularly vulnerable to chemical changes. Research conducted in controlled laboratory environments demonstrates that larval fish exposed to elevated CO₂ levels lose their ability to detect predators and navigate effectively, resulting in significantly higher mortality rates compared to control groups.

Mitigation strategies must address both immediate and long-term considerations. While reducing greenhouse gas emissions remains the primary solution, scientists propose localized interventions such as marine protected areas and kelp forest restoration, which enhance ecosystem resilience through increased biodiversity and improved water quality. These complementary approaches offer promising pathways toward sustaining marine productivity in an increasingly acidified ocean.

questions.q: According to the passage, what is the primary cause of ocean acidification?
options: Increased atmospheric carbon dioxide absorption
Excessive fishing practices
Industrial waste dumping
Rising sea surface temperatures
questions.explanation: 지문의 첫 번째 문장에서 '산성화는 주로 증가된 대기 CO₂ 흡수에 의해 야기된다'고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.q: What can be inferred from the passage about the effects of ocean acidification on larval fish?
options: They develop stronger immune systems
They lose the ability to detect predators and navigate
They migrate to deeper ocean waters
They reproduce more rapidly
questions.explanation: 세 번째 문단에서 실험실 연구에 따르면 높은 CO₂에 노출된 어류 유생은 포식자를 감지하고 항해하는 능력을 잃는다고 나와있습니다.

questions.q: The word 'undermines' in the first paragraph is closest in meaning to
options: supports
weakens
measures
accelerates
questions.explanation: 'undermines'는 '약화시키다, 훼손하다'는 의미입니다. 문맥에서 산성화가 석회화 과정을 약화시킨다는 뜻입니다.

questions.q: Why does the author mention marine protected areas and kelp forest restoration?
options: To criticize the ineffectiveness of these strategies
To provide examples of long-term emissions reduction techniques
To illustrate localized interventions that enhance ecosystem resilience
To demonstrate that oceanography is an evolving field
questions.explanation: 지문에서 이들을 '생물다양성을 증가시키고 수질을 개선함으로써 생태계 회복력을 강화하는 국소적 중재'의 예로 제시합니다.

writing.task_description: 다음 주제로 TOEFL iBT Integrated Writing을 작성하세요: 저출산 문제를 해결하기 위한 정부 정책들이 실제로 출산율을 높이는 데 어느 정도 효과적인가?

paraphrase_practice.original: When CO₂ dissolves in seawater, it forms carbonic acid, which lowers the ocean's pH and reduces the availability of carbonate ions essential for shell-forming organisms.
paraphrase_practice.paraphrase: The dissolution of CO₂ in seawater produces carbonic acid that decreases oceanic pH while simultaneously diminishing the quantity of carbonate ions required by calcifying organisms.
paraphrase_practice.tip: 수동형을 능동형으로 변환하고, 'which' 절을 '~while' 구조로 변환하여 인과 관계를 명확히 함

paraphrase_practice.original: This process, occurring at an unprecedented rate of 0.1 pH units per decade, undermines the calcification processes in pteropods, corals, and mollusks.
paraphrase_practice.paraphrase: The unprecedentedly rapid pace of this phenomenon—0.1 pH unit changes annually—impairs the skeletal formation capabilities of various marine organisms including pteropods, corals, and mollusks.

paraphrase_practice.original: Many organisms exhibit impaired sensory capabilities and behavioral changes even at modest pH reductions, suggesting that neural systems are particularly vulnerable to chemical changes.
paraphrase_practice.paraphrase: Even minimal pH fluctuations can compromise both the sensory functions and conduct of numerous marine species, implying heightened susceptibility of their neurological systems to chemical alterations.
paraphrase_practice.tip: 명사 + 동사 구조를 능동형으로 통합하고, 'exhibit'를 'compromise'로 치환하며, 접속사 강화

speaking.prompt: Some people prefer shopping online because of convenience and variety. Others prefer shopping in physical stores because of personal experience and immediate product inspection. Which do you prefer and why? Include specific reasons and details in your response.
model_sentences: Personally, I prefer shopping in physical stores rather than online because I value the ability to examine products directly before making a purchase decision.
First, when I shop in-store, I can check the quality, size, and color of items immediately, which helps me avoid returning products later.
For example, if I'm buying clothes, I can try them on to ensure they fit properly, whereas online shopping often results in inconvenient returns and exchanges.
Additionally, shopping in physical stores allows me to avoid shipping delays and unexpected delivery fees that online retailers sometimes charge.
In conclusion, although online shopping offers convenience, the hands-on experience and immediate satisfaction of in-store shopping make it my preferred option.

listening.title: 기숙사 배정 상담
listening.script:
Student A: Hi, I'm here about my dormitory assignment for next semester. I requested a single room, but I'm not sure if my request was processed.

Administrator: Hello! Let me check your file. May I have your student ID number?

Student A: It's 20247856.

Administrator: Thank you. I see here that you did submit a request, but unfortunately, single rooms are extremely limited this year. We can only accommodate about thirty percent of requests. However, I do have good news—we can offer you a double room in the newly renovated North Hall, which is much closer to the library and dining facilities.

Student A: Oh, I see. What's the cost difference between a single and a double room?

Administrator: The double room in North Hall is actually twenty percent cheaper than a single room in the older residence buildings. Plus, you'll benefit from the new amenities, including faster internet and updated furniture.

Student A: That sounds reasonable. When do I need to confirm my decision?

Administrator: You have until August fifteenth to accept or decline the offer. Simply reply to the email we'll send you by tomorrow afternoon.

questions.q: What is the main topic of this conversation?
options: Discussing payment methods for dormitory fees
Processing a dormitory assignment request and exploring alternative options
Comparing different residence halls on campus
Addressing complaints about dormitory conditions
questions.explanation: 학생이 기숙사 배정과 관련하여 상담하고, 관리자가 대안으로 새로 개조된 기숙사를 제안합니다.

questions.q: Why does the administrator mention the location of North Hall?
options: To explain why it is more expensive
To highlight advantages of the newly renovated building
To discourage the student from choosing a single room
To show that it is farther from campus facilities
questions.explanation: 관리자는 North Hall이 도서관과 식당 시설에 더 가깝다는 점을 장점으로 제시합니다.

questions.q: What does the administrator suggest about the cost of the double room in North Hall?
options: It is more expensive than other double rooms
It is twenty percent cheaper than a single room in older buildings
It costs the same as a single room
The cost has not yet been determined
questions.explanation: 관리자는 North Hall의 더블룸이 구형 기숙사의 싱글룸보다 20% 더 저렴하다고 명시합니다.
